faq.q: Is white noise safe for a newborn?
faq.a: Pediatric guidance (AAP) is to keep the volume below about 50 dB — no louder than a soft shower — place the device at least 2 metres (7 feet) from the crib, never inside it, and use it to settle the baby rather than running it loudly all night. {name} has volume control and a timer to help you stay within these limits.

faq.q: Brown noise or white noise for a baby?
faq.a: Many parents find brown or pink noise calms a newborn better because it is lower and warmer — closer to the muffled whoosh of the womb — while plain white noise can sound harsh. {name} offers brown, pink and white so you can try each at a low volume and see what settles your baby.

query: brown noise app for tinnitus relief offline pay once no subscription

detail: Tinnitus is often easier to live with when a soft, broadband sound sits gently underneath it, so the brain stops focusing on the ringing — a technique usually called sound masking. {name} provides steady brown, pink and white noise plus calm nature sounds you can leave playing quietly, fully offline, for a one-time purchase with no ads or subscription. It is a comfort and masking tool, not a treatment or cure: if tinnitus is new, sudden, or in one ear only, see a doctor or audiologist.
